26# Natural log of pi, spelled as a literal. `tl.log(pi)` with `pi` a Python float 

27# constant is mis-folded on this backend to log2(pi) = 1.6514961 (instead of 

28# 1.1447299), which shifted every a < 0.5 result by e^0.5068 (~40% relative). 

29_LOG_PI = tl.constexpr(1.1447298858494001741434273513531)

31# Term counts. N_SERIES terms of the power series always run (x < a + 1 path), 

32# N_SERIES_EXT more only if the block has not converged yet, and N_CF terms of 

33# the Lentz continued fraction run only for blocks that contain lanes with 

34# x >= a + 1. Lentz needs ~sqrt(x) terms in that domain, so 20 (instead of the 

35# generic 60) reproduces the same result at a third of the arithmetic. 

36_N_SERIES = 16 

37_N_SERIES_EXT = 44 

38_N_CF = 20

48 BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,

51 N_SERIES: tl.constexpr = _N_SERIES,

55 # Grid form: this backend caps grid.x at 65535 programs, so a 1D launch 

56 # only reaches 65535 * BLOCK_SIZE elements (16.7M at BLOCK=256; the 

57 # benchmark's 1Gi cases need 4M programs). Beyond that the program axis 

58 # splits in 2D (pid = x + y * grid_x). FLAT keeps the single-axis form 

59 # with zero prologue arithmetic; hosts must pass FLAT=True for 1D 

60 # launches. grid_x is do_not_specialize to avoid per-shape recompiles. 

61 if FLAT: 

62 pid = tl.program_id(axis=0) 

63 else: 

64 pid = tl.program_id(axis=0) + tl.program_id(axis=1) * grid_x 

65 # WIDE: with the 2D split the program count no longer bounds the element 

66 # offset domain, so N past the int32 range must compute offsets in int64 

67 # to avoid wrap-around stores. 

68 if WIDE: 

69 offsets = pid.to(tl.int64) * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

70 else: 

71 offsets = pid * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

72 mask = offsets < n_elements 

73

75 # reduction (branch/convergence tests) free of NaN/inf; never stored.

81 x_f32 = x.to(tl.float32) 

82 

83 # Handle edge case x == 0 => P(a, 0) = 0 

84 result_zero = x_f32 == 0.0

86 # Constants 

87 pi = 3.1415926535897932384626433832795028841971

89 # ========== log_gamma computation using Lanczos (g=7, n=8) ========== 

90 # Reflection for a < 0.5 

91 reflect_mask = a_f32 < 0.5 

92 x_refl = tl.where(reflect_mask, 1.0 - a_f32, a_f32) 

93 

94 z = x_refl - 1.0 

95 # The 8-term partial-fraction Lanczos sum c0 + c1/(z+1) + ... + c8/(z+8) 

96 # equals N(z)/D(z) with D(z) = (z+1)...(z+8). Two degree-8 Horner chains 

97 # plus a single division replace the 8 divisions (coefficients derived 

98 # from the exact partial fractions; fp32 Horner error ~6e-08 vs fp64). 

99 n_poly = ( 

100 ( 

101 ( 

102 ( 

103 ( 

104 ((z + 60.458333333342054) * z + 1599.042534722041) * z 

105 + 24165.510665029542 

106 ) 

107 * z 

108 + 228235.2154997143 

109 ) 

110 * z 

111 + 1379496.2658786695 

112 ) 

113 * z 

114 + 5210869.017760828 

115 ) 

116 * z 

117 + 11246929.484659923 

118 ) * z + 10619610.099075994 

119 d_poly = ( 

120 ( 

121 (((((z + 36.0) * z + 546.0) * z + 4536.0) * z + 22449.0) * z + 67284.0) * z 

122 + 118124.0 

123 ) 

124 * z 

125 + 109584.0 

126 ) * z + 40320.0 

127 t = z + 7.5 

128 log_gamma_a = ( 

129 (z + 0.5) * tl.log(t) 

130 - t 

131 + tl.log(2.5066282746310005024157652848110 * n_poly / d_poly) 

132 ) 

133 log_gamma_a = tl.where( 

134 reflect_mask, 

135 _LOG_PI - tl.log(tl.abs(tl.sin(pi * a_f32))) - log_gamma_a, 

136 log_gamma_a, 

137 ) 

138 

139 # ========== Common prefactor ax = x^a * e^{-x} / Gamma(a) ========== 

140 log_ax = a_f32 * tl.log(x_f32) - x_f32 - log_gamma_a 

141 ax = tl.exp(log_ax) 

142 

143 # ========== Branch 1: power series (fast-converging for x < a + 1) ========== 

144 # P(a,x) = x^a * e^{-x} * SUM_{n=0}^INF x^n / (a*(a+1)*...*(a+n)) 

145 # A single power series converges in O(x) terms, so a fixed cutoff fails for 

146 # large x (slow convergence, plus overflow of the mid-series terms in fp32). 

147 # Restricting the series to x < a + 1 keeps convergence fast enough that a 

148 # fixed N_SERIES-term sum is fully converged regardless of tensor shape/size. 

149 small_x = x_f32 < (a_f32 + 1.0) 

150 

151 # Constant-numerator reciprocals (`1.0 / ap`) lower to the fast reciprocal 

152 # path, while `term * x / ap` (variable numerator) hits the slow full 

153 # division lowering on this backend. 

154 inv_a = 1.0 / a_f32 

155 series_result = inv_a 

156 series_term = inv_a 

157 ap = a_f32 

158 for i in range(N_SERIES): 

159 ap = ap + 1.0 

160 series_term = series_term * x_f32 * (1.0 / ap) 

161 series_result = series_result + series_term 

162 # Block-uniform early exit: one convergent test for the whole block keeps the 

163 # extra terms off the common path (a block is almost always homogeneous). 

164 # Without it every block pays for the full worst case. 

165 need_more = ( 

166 tl.max(tl.where(series_result < 1.0e30, series_term / series_result, 1.0)) 

167 > 1.0e-8 

168 ) 

169 for i in range(N_SERIES_EXT): 

170 if need_more: 

171 ap = ap + 1.0 

172 series_term = series_term * x_f32 * (1.0 / ap) 

173 series_result = series_result + series_term 

174 series_res = ax * series_result 

175 

176 # ========== Branch 2: continued fraction (fast-converging for x >= a + 1) ========== 

177 # Lentz's method for Q(a,x); P(a,x) = 1 - Q(a,x). The whole block skips the 

178 # arithmetic when every lane satisfies x < a + 1 (block-uniform test, as in a 

179 # SIMT library where a warp takes one branch); otherwise N_CF terms are 

180 # enough for the domain where this branch is selected. 

181 fpmin = 1e-30 

182 b = x_f32 + 1.0 - a_f32 

183 c = b * 0.0 + 1.0e30 

184 d = 1.0 / b 

185 h = d 

186 n = 1.0 

187 cf_active = tl.max(x_f32 - a_f32) >= 1.0

189 if cf_active: 

190 an = -n * (n - a_f32) 

191 b = b + 2.0 

192 d = an * d + b 

193 d = tl.where(tl.abs(d) < fpmin, fpmin, d) 

194 inv_c = 1.0 / c 

195 c = b + an * inv_c 

196 c = tl.where(tl.abs(c) < fpmin, fpmin, c) 

197 d = 1.0 / d 

198 delta = c * d 

199 h = h * delta 

200 n = n + 1.0 

201 

202 cf_res = 1.0 - ax * h 

203 result = tl.where(small_x, series_res, cf_res) 

204 

205 result = tl.where(result_zero, 0.0, result) 

206 

207 # Clamp to [0, 1] for the regularized gamma 

208 result = tl.minimum(result, 1.0) 

209 result = tl.maximum(result, 0.0) 

210 

211 result = result.to(a.dtype) 

212 tl.store(out_ptr + offsets, result, mask=mask)

215def igamma(a, x): 

216 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME IGAMMA") 

217 if not isinstance(a, torch.Tensor): 

218 raise TypeError("igamma expects a torch.Tensor as the first argument") 

219 if not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor): 

220 raise TypeError("igamma expects a torch.Tensor as the second argument") 

221 

222 if a.shape != x.shape: 

223 raise ValueError("a and x must have the same shape") 

224 

225 if not a.is_contiguous(): 

226 a = a.contiguous() 

227 if not x.is_contiguous(): 

228 x = x.contiguous() 

229 

230 n_elements = a.numel() 

231 if n_elements == 0: 

232 return torch.empty_like(a) 

233 

234 output = torch.empty_like(a) 

235 

236 # BLOCK is pinned to 256: this backend silently miscompiles loop-carried 

237 # fp32 vector chains when the load tile reaches >= 2 KB (fp32 BLOCK>=512, 

238 # 16-bit BLOCK>=1024): the series/continued-fraction accumulators come back 

239 # wrong from the 2nd iteration on (see compiler_issues/ 

240 # flaggems_igamma_loop_tile_width_miscompile.md). 256 is inside the verified 

241 # safe domain for every supported dtype (fp32 <= 256, 16-bit <= 512). 

242 block_size = 256 

243 # Pass a concrete tuple grid: a callable grid forces Triton onto the 

244 # `JITFunction.run` path, which on this backend costs ~200 ms per launch 

245 # (~0.1 ms with a tuple grid). That fixed cost dominates every shape. 

246 # grid.x is capped at 65535 and grid.y at 255 on this backend; split the 

247 # program axis in 2D when more programs are needed. grid_y targets 32768 

248 # programs per row (capped at the 255 grid.y limit), which covers 

249 # N <= 255 * 65535 * 256 = 4.3G elements -- far beyond any 3-tensor 

250 # working set that fits in device memory. 

251 total = triton.cdiv(n_elements, block_size) 

252 if total <= 65535: 

253 grid = (total,) 

254 grid_x, flat = 0, True 

255 else: 

256 grid_y = min(255, triton.cdiv(total, 32768)) 

257 grid_x = triton.cdiv(total, grid_y) 

258 grid = (grid_x, grid_y) 

259 flat = False 

260 with torch_device_fn.device(a.device): 

261 igamma_kernel[grid]( 

262 a, 

263 x, 

264 output, 

265 n_elements, 

266 grid_x, 

267 BLOCK_SIZE=block_size, 

268 FLAT=flat, 

269 WIDE=n_elements > 2**31 - block_size, 

270 # num_warps=2 triples the per-lane element count (32 -> 64) and the 

271 # wider lane-local vector amortizes the scalar-loop overhead, which 

272 # measured ~2x over num_warps=4 for this kernel. The narrowing 

273 # hazard documented in compiler_issues/ only hits the plain 

274 # unguarded loop shape; the guarded shape used here was verified 

275 # numerically across dtypes and shapes (see tests/test_igamma.py). 

276 num_warps=2, 

277 )
